message.content:
Based on the search results, here is a comprehensive overview of **calcium-containing foods**:

## Dairy Products (Highest Natural Sources)

Dairy products are among the most concentrated and best-absorbed sources of calcium:

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Yogurt, plain low-fat (8 oz) | 415 mg |
| Milk, nonfat (1 cup) | 299 mg |
| Milk, whole (1 cup) | 276 mg |
| Mozzarella, part-skim (1.5 oz) | 333 mg |
| Cheddar cheese (1.5 oz) | 306 mg |
| Cottage cheese, 1% fat (1 cup) | 138 mg |

## Fish (with Bones)

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Sardines, canned in oil with bones (3 oz) | 325 mg |
| Salmon, pink canned with bones (3 oz) | 181 mg |

## Plant-Based & Non-Dairy Sources

### Leafy Green Vegetables
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Collard greens, cooked (1 cup) | 324 mg |
| Kale, cooked (1 cup) | 177-94 mg |
| Bok choy (1 cup) | 74-158 mg |
| Turnip greens, boiled (½ cup) | 99 mg |
| Broccoli, raw (½ cup) | 21 mg |

**Note:** Spinach contains high levels of oxalic acid, which binds calcium and reduces absorption to only about 5%. Kale, broccoli, and bok choy have better calcium bioavailability.

### Legumes & Soy Products
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Tofu, firm with calcium sulfate (½ cup) | 253 mg |
| Tofu, soft with calcium sulfate (½ cup) | 138 mg |
| Edamame, cooked (1 cup) | 130 mg |
| Soybeans, cooked (½ cup) | 131 mg |

### Nuts & Seeds
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Chia seeds (1 tablespoon) | 76 mg |
| Almonds (1 oz) | 76 mg |
| Sesame seeds/tahini (1 tbsp) | 64 mg |

### Fortified Foods
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Calcium-fortified orange juice (1 cup) | 349 mg |
| Fortified soy milk (1 cup) | 299 mg |
| Fortified almond milk (1 cup) | 482 mg |
| Fortified breakfast cereals (1 serving) | 100-1,000 mg |

### Other Sources
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Dried figs (4) | 54 mg |
| Oranges (1 medium) | 60-65 mg |
| Blackberries (1 cup) | 42 mg |

## Key Facts About Calcium Absorption

- **Dairy products and fortified foods**: ~30% absorption rate
- **Certain plant foods** (spinach, chard, rhubarb): Much lower absorption due to oxalic acid
- **Kale, broccoli, bok choy**: Similar absorption to milk because they contain lower oxalate levels
- **Vitamin D** is essential for proper calcium absorption

Adults generally need **1,000-1,200 mg of calcium per day**, depending on age and sex.

Sources:
1. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/
2. https://www.health.harvard.edu/nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
3. https://www.webmd.com/food-recipes/guide/calcium-vitamin-d-foods
4. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK45523/table/ch7.t2/
5. https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-calcium
6. https://gp-training.hee.nhs.uk/windsor/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2021/09/Vitamin-D-testing-and-treatment-guidelines.pdf
7. https://imsear.searo.who.int/bitstreams/99ce16a3-83a5-4fba-8f33-d0c9a0428303/download
8. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_307FM.pdf
9. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_834FM.pdf?uid=598797444&uid2=2020111220184122
